title: These Are the Best iPhone Duo Cases and Accessories I’ve Tried
gist: Wired's Simon Hill reviews early cases and accessories for Apple's first folding phone, the iPhone Duo, concluding that the hinge is the hardest part to protect and that most current MagSafe accessories are designed for regular iPhones and only partly fit the foldable. The piece also documents the Duo's charging specs (60W wired, 25W Qi2 wireless).

insights.claim: Apple's iPhone Duo is Apple's first folding phone, costs 'a couple grand', is easy to drop when opened one-handed, and any repair can be very pricey, making protective cases a near-mandatory add-on purchase.
insights.speaker: Simon Hill
insights.so_what: An expensive, fragile foldable creates a sizeable attach-rate opportunity for case and accessory makers.
insights.quote: If you’ve spent a couple grand on Apple’s first folding phone, you should really protect it with one of the best iPhone Duo cases.

insights.claim: Making cases for foldable phones is challenging, the hinge is the hardest part to protect, and many early iPhone Duo cases are two-piece designs relying on adhesive for the front half, which the reviewer found tends to come loose and leave the hinge exposed.
insights.speaker: Simon Hill
insights.so_what: Case makers that solve hinge protection without adhesive can differentiate in the foldable accessory market.
insights.quote: no case is perfect, and the hinge is tricky to protect
insights.locator: All that said, no case is perfect

insights.claim: Wired's top iPhone Duo case pick is the $55 Dbrand Grip Case, followed by Moft's $70 Dynamic Folio as best stand case, Mous' $90 Limitless Case as best slim case and Smartish's $50 Gripzilla as best thick case.
insights.speaker: Simon Hill
insights.so_what: Shows price points ($50-$90) and which accessory brands are winning early foldable-iPhone placement.
insights.locator: Best Case / Best Stand Case / Best Slim Case / Best Thick Case

insights.claim: The UAG Mouve XTE ($85) and Aulumu Aduo Particle ($90) iPhone Duo cases are not recommended because they rely on adhesive and offer no hinge protection; the reviewer calls the UAG case a rare misfire for the brand.
insights.speaker: Simon Hill
insights.so_what: Early product misses by established brands can cost share in a new device category's accessory cycle.
insights.quote: It’s a rare misfire for the brand.

insights.claim: The iPhone Duo supports wired charging up to 60 watts (requiring a USB PD 3.2 AVS charger rated 60W+) and wireless charging up to 25 watts via Qi2 25W; other chargers work but more slowly.
insights.speaker: Simon Hill
insights.so_what: Qi2 25W and USB PD 3.2 AVS compatibility becomes a selling point for charger makers like Anker, Nomad and Belkin.
insights.quote: Apple’s iPhone Duo supports wired charging at up to 60 watts and wireless charging at up to 25 watts

insights.claim: Existing MagSafe wallets and power banks, such as UAG's Metropolis wallet and Anker's MagGo 2 Pro power bank, are designed for regular iPhones and extend beyond the bottom edge of the iPhone Duo, signalling an unaddressed gap for foldable-specific accessories.
insights.speaker: Simon Hill
insights.so_what: Watch for accessory makers launching Duo-specific form factors to fill the fit gap.
insights.quote: All the MagSafe wallets I’ve tried are designed for regular iPhones

insights.claim: The iPhone Duo can pair only with the Apple Pencil (USB-C) for writing and sketching on its cover or inner display; it does not support the Apple Pencil Pro or other Pencil models.
insights.speaker: Simon Hill
insights.so_what: Pencil support positions the foldable partly as a notebook device, but limited model compatibility narrows the upsell.
insights.quote: Sadly, it doesn’t support the Apple Pencil Pro or other models
